roles.heroLead: Up here the weather tests everything, and a shower is no exception — tile and grout shrug water off, but only a bonded membrane actually stops it. Skip that layer and a North Bend bathroom quietly becomes a framing repair. We build the assembly, flood it for 24 hours, photograph it holding, then tile.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in North Bend, WA?
roles.costP1: In North Bend, installed tile runs about $14–$26 per square foot once tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor are tallied; labor starts at $11/sq ft by itself. Tub-shower surrounds go $3,200–$6,800, a ~45 sq ft bathroom floor $900–$1,600, and a complete bathroom — floor, shower and niche together — usually $6,500–$14,000.
roles.costP2: Format is the lever most people miss. Installing a $4 mosaic can outprice installing a $12 large-format porcelain plank, since every cut and every grout joint is labor — the receipt from the tile aisle is the smaller half of the story.
roles.costNote: Upper-valley ranges as of August 2026, covering tile, materials and labor together. The free on-site estimate produces the written number that holds.
roles.layersLead: Count seven layers from subfloor to grout. Each failed shower we tear into skipped at least one — the membrane, almost every time — and the few hundred dollars it saved became a five-figure demolition.
roles.whyP1: A leak never knocks. Water sneaks through grout, soaks the substrate, and only after a winter or two does the evidence appear — a soft spot in the hall, a ring on the ceiling below. By then the job list reads framing, subfloor, drywall and tile, all over again.
roles.whyP2: About a tenth of what a shower costs is the waterproofing. Deleting that tenth is the costliest decision a remodel can make.

roles.cardFloors: Mudrooms, entries, kitchens, baths and basements — floors that meet ski boots and firewood. Subfloor brought flat first, uncoupling membrane wherever movement or radiant heat calls for it.

roles.cardDemo: Old tile, thinset and backer stripped and gone — dust held back with sheeting and negative air, debris hauled off the property, not staged by the woodpile.

roles.faqH2: Tile installation FAQ — North Bend, WA
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in North Bend, WA?
roles.faqA1: Tile installation in North Bend prices at $14 to $26 per square foot installed, taking in the tile, its setting materials, substrate prep and labor — with labor alone from $11 per square foot. A typical tub-shower surround costs $3,200 to $6,800; a full bathroom holding floor, shower and niche finishes between $6,500 and $14,000. The format you pick moves cost more than the tile's sticker: mosaics and large-format each demand well more labor per foot than basic 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in North Bend?
roles.faqA2: $3,200 to $6,800 covers a standard alcove shower in North Bend — tear-out, bonded waterproofing, a pre-sloped pan or base, tile work, niche and grout included. Curbless entries, benches, steam builds and full-height stone land above that. The waterproofing is about a tenth of the price and the whole reason the other nine-tenths survive.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes — it's the one step that never gets skipped. Every shower gets a bonded system behind the tile: a pre-sloped base, an ANSI A118.10 membrane in sheet or liquid form taken up the walls, corners, seams and pipe penetrations all sealed, and a full 24-hour flood test photographed before setting begins. Tile and grout only slow water down; stopping it is the membrane's job alone.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Give a North Bend bathroom four to six working days: demolition with dust protection, then substrate and waterproofing capped by the 24-hour flood test, one to two days of tile setting, and a closing day of grout, silicone and trim. The grout wants 24 more hours to cure before the first shower. A floor on its own is a one-to-two-day project.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Porcelain for floors, showers and any surface that gets wet or worked hard — it's denser, chips less and absorbs under 0.5% water, which matters in a house where boots come in wet half the year. Ceramic serves well on walls and backsplashes for less money. Our North Bend rule: porcelain underfoot, always; ceramic and glass up top where they belong.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes, and at this end of the valley it's the upgrade with the best cost-to-comfort ratio going: $11 to $16 a square foot installed with the thermostat. The mat lies over an uncoupling membrane, is resistance-tested before the tile goes down and once more after, and draws from a dedicated circuit. It only makes financial sense while the floor is already open — plan it into the remodel, not after.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually. Old tile demo with haul-away starts at $3.50 per square foot, and it's the only way to truly inspect the subfloor for rot and movement and to keep finished heights right at the doors. A sound, flat, firmly bonded existing floor can sometimes take new tile on top, but the height goes up and the unknowns stay buried — we'd rather meet them at demo than after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in North Bend?
roles.faqA8: For a standard 30 square foot kitchen, a North Bend backsplash installs at $1,100 to $2,200 — outlet openings cut in, edges finished with trim, grout tuned to the counter. Mosaic sheets, herringbone runs, a framed feature behind the stove and ceiling-height slab-look porcelain sit at the top end, because the hours live in layout and cutting.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often, yes. From $8 per square foot we repair and regrout: stained or crumbling grout, the odd cracked tile from something dropped, corners where the old grout should give way to silicone. If tiles ring hollow, let go in a spreading pattern, or the wall flexes, the substrate underneath has failed — a repair there only rents time. You'll hear which diagnosis is yours before we price anything.
roles.faqQ10: Which North Bend neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: The whole upper valley — downtown North Bend, Si View, Forster Woods, Tanner, Riverbend, Wilderness Rim, Cedar Falls, Edgewick, Maloney Grove and Sallal Prairie — plus Snoqualmie, Snoqualmie Ridge, Fall City, Preston and on up toward Snoqualmie Pass. Ernie's Grove and the far side of the valley too; just say where you are.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: OC Flooring warranties tile workmanship for 2 years — noticeably longer than our carpet coverage, since tile defects tend to show in the second year, not the second week. Full bonded waterproofing assemblies also carry their manufacturer's warranty when we install the complete system. Membrane and flood test get photographed, so the documentation outlives the remodel and travels with the house.
